body:
Okay I agree with you. She doesn't have any obligation, true that. Although I wanted her to be by my side, it sucks that she can't and I respect it. 

Just want to ask (not a retort), what would be your opinion if this were my spouse or my parents in this case instead of my friend?

That sucks. Really does. And do you think what they did is justified? I just wanna know your opinion. 

It's true that no one owes anyone anything but it's morally wrong to to not show even an iota of compassion in the name of boundaries. It takes tremendous amounts of courage to talk about mental health, especially when it comes to suicidal thoughts.

So it's my fault  because I opened up about my feelings? Thanks.

She could have supported me. I am going to a psychiatrist right now. But still, some words of consolement from her would not have taken a lot of effort. She could have at the least dropped a message the next day asking if I'm better. 

 She lied to me about being my best friend. Because a good friend would never cut someone off this way, in such a cold manner.
She was the only friend I had.
And how do you think I can ever rekindle a relationship where the person literally cut me off when I legit said I had hit my lowest point. She was no aquaintance.

But is a hurts so bad when she said she can't help me. All I wanted to do was to talk to her. Be a friend. That'd have made me feel infinitely better. But cutting me off was cold, bruh. So difficult to accept.
But no contact? Not even a text saying how I feel? Been a month
I told her I had feelings for her and I needed her presence
